summary: Proposes an extensible monitoring framework for RTP that adds new RTCP Extended Report block types to report media quality metrics. It recommends that a new XR block carry a single metric or a small related group. It gives guidelines for those who define such blocks. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6792 explains how to add quality measurements to reports about real-time audio and video. It recommends small report blocks that different applications can reuse.

questions: how to define new rtcp metrics

how do i monitor rtp stream quality
subtitle: Guidelines for small, reusable quality reports carried by RTCP Extended Reports.

tldr.problem: RTP applications need quality measurements, but application-specific report blocks can fragment the design and weaken interoperability.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recommends small RTCP XR blocks for one metric or a closely related set, with guidance on payload types, correlation and shared measurement information.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6792 is an Informational framework for defining metrics blocks; it defines no normative requirements and has not been updated or obsoleted in the supplied metadata.

facts.label: Metric block guidance
facts.value: One metric or a small related set

today: RFC 6792 is an Informational memo published in November 2012. The supplied metadata lists no later RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: Why RTP Monitoring Needs Shared Design
sections.content:
Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) applications use measurements to understand transmission quality. The RTP Control Protocol (RTCP), including its Extended Reports (XR), can carry these measurements during a session.

The memo warns that many application-specific blocks can make implementations less interoperable. It describes a framework for reporting reusable quality-of-service and quality-of-experience measurements.
sections.plainLanguage: RTP carries real-time media, and RTCP carries reports about that media. Shared report designs let different applications use the same measurements.

sections.title: Types of Monitoring Measurements
sections.content:
Transport-level metrics describe packet loss, packet delay and jitter. Application-level metrics describe application quality or the user's end-to-end experience, while end-system metrics describe how a terminal handles transport problems.

The memo also distinguishes direct metrics from measurements taken over an interval, accumulated over time or sampled at a particular instant. These categories describe what a measurement represents and how it is collected.
sections.plainLanguage: Some measurements describe the network, some describe application quality, and some describe how a device handles network problems. A measurement can cover one reporting period, build up over time, or record a moment.

sections.title: Monitors and RTP Metrics Blocks
sections.content:
The framework has two parts: a monitor that gathers information and an RTP Metrics Block that carries it. A monitor can run at an endpoint, an intermediate RTP system, or a third-party observer.

RTCP and RTCP XR carry monitoring information between participants. A monitor can also export collected metrics to a network-management system using a non-RTP method.
sections.plainLanguage: A monitor collects measurements, and a metrics block carries them in a report. The monitor can be part of an endpoint, an intermediate system or a separate observer.

sections.title: Guidelines for Defining Report Blocks
sections.content:
A new metrics block should contain one metric or a small number of metrics about one concern. This lets applications combine the blocks they need and makes each block easier to reuse across applications.

A block whose interpretation depends on the media codec should include its payload type. When reports need to match non-RTP information, the memo recommends carrying correlation information in an RTCP SDES item; shared measurement details can be reported once in a Measurement Information Block when applicable.
sections.plainLanguage: Keep each report block focused so applications can reuse it. State the media format when a measurement depends on it, and use shared fields to connect related reports.

sections.title: Protecting Monitoring Reports
sections.content:
The memo says RTCP XR extensions do not add security vulnerabilities beyond those described for RTCP XR. Monitoring still needs consideration because an intermediate RTP system may forward reports to other systems.

If a report contains sensitive information, the memo says it should receive the same protection as the RTP flows it measures. A third-party monitor should discard an encrypted report if local policy does not allow the receiving system to decrypt and forward it.
sections.plainLanguage: Monitoring reports can reveal information about a session. Protect sensitive reports as carefully as the media they describe.
